title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array Alternating
summary: Given a 0-indexed array nums consisting of n positive integers, determine the minimum number of operations required to make the array alternating.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array nums consisting of n positive integers, determine the minimum number of operations required to make the array alternating. An array is considered alternating if: - nums[i - 2] == nums[i] for all 2 <= i <= n - 1. - nums[i - 1] != nums[i] for all 1 <= i <= n - 1. In one operation, you can change any element nums[i] to any positive integer. Return the minimum number of such operations needed to achieve the alternating array.
constraints: All even indices must share one value and all odd indices must share another.
The chosen even and odd values must differ.
One operation may change any element to any positive integer.
reference_solution:
def minimum_alternating_changes(nums):
    if len(nums)<2:return 0
    from collections import Counter
    even=Counter(nums[::2]).most_common(2)+[(None,0),(None,0)]
    odd=Counter(nums[1::2]).most_common(2)+[(None,0),(None,0)]
    if even[0][0]!=odd[0][0]:kept=even[0][1]+odd[0][1]
    else:kept=max(even[0][1]+odd[1][1],even[1][1]+odd[0][1])
    return len(nums)-kept

hints: Only the retained counts for one even value and one different odd value matter.
The optimal choice uses one of the two most common values on each parity.
Take both top frequencies when their values differ; otherwise try replacing either side with its runner-up.
If the top values conflict, any value below second place cannot improve the retained total compared with that side’s runner-up.

Choose 1 for even positions and 2 for odd positions, changing the two later even values.
